method: HS-SPME-GC-MS/MS (DVB/CAR/PDMS 50/30um 2cm; 30 degC, 20 min equil + 30 min extract; DB-WAX UI 30m; EI full scan m/z 33-300 + timed SIM; MRM for S-analytes)
sample_prep: 10 mL into pre-salted 20 mL vial (3.0 g NaCl), H3PO4 to pH 2.5, 50 uL 1 mM EDTA, ISTD mix, crimp under argon
decision_informed: Does the volatile profile differ by ARM? Supplies the mechanistic covariates the sensory panel's discrimination result is regressed on.

method: HS-SPME-GC-MS/MS, as-is aliquot (EDTA, argon headspace, NO reductant, NO ascorbate)
sample_prep: Aliquot split A of the V1 vial set
decision_informed: Numerator of the oxidation index. Free thiol is what the nose smells.

method: Identical to V2 after 1 mM TCEP, 30 min at 25 degC under argon (reduces disulfides back to thiols)
sample_prep: Aliquot split B, TCEP added immediately on opening
decision_informed: Denominator of the oxidation index. Separates 'thiol was oxidised' from 'thiol was never there / was stripped'.

method: (V3 - V2) / V3, computed per analyte; orthogonally confirmed by direct DFDS and DMDS peak areas from V1
analytes: Disulfide-bound fraction of FFT and of methanethiol
decision_informed: THE PRIMARY ENDPOINT. Responds to OXYGEN EXPOSURE specifically, not to elapsed time. Separates 'the inert flush failed' (index high early) from 'the product is simply old' (index low, absolute thiol falling). Gate for admitting a batch to the sensory panel.

method: PFBBr derivatisation (pentafluorobenzyl bromide, alkaline, under argon, EDTA present) -> PFB-thioether, GC-NCI-MS SIM
sample_prep: Only triggered if V2 LOQ >5 ng/L in method validation
decision_informed: Contingency only. NOTE: measures FREE thiol only and the alkaline step itself drives thiol->disulfide, so it must always be run paired with a TCEP arm; it cannot replace V2/V3.

method: HPLC-DAD 325 nm, C18 150x4.6 mm 2.7 um, 0.1% formic acid / methanol gradient, 25 degC
sample_prep: 1 mL, 0.45 um PVDF, dilute 1:5 in 0.1% formic acid, -80 degC, analyse <=14 d
decision_informed: Extraction equivalence between arms (are we comparing the same coffee?) and the CQA side of the lactone ratio.

method: Same run as N1, 325 nm, separate calibrants
sample_prep: SAME aliquot as N1 but acidified to pH 2.5-3.0 AT THE MOMENT OF OPENING and held <=4 degC. Lactones hydrolyse back to CQAs in aqueous solution at a pH- and T-dependent rate, so an un-quenched sample reports storage-independent artefact.
decision_informed: Bitterness precursor drift. REPORT AS lactone:CQA RATIO, never absolute. A spiked 3-CQL handling control runs in every sequence to quantify handling-induced hydrolysis.

method: HPLC-DAD 272 nm (caffeine) / 264 nm (trigonelline), same column as N1
decision_informed: EXTRACTION-CONSISTENCY MARKER. Caffeine is thermally and oxidatively inert over 48 h, so any between-arm difference is a brewing artefact, not a treatment effect. This is the assay that vetoes a batch.

method: HPLC-RID/UV 210 nm on ion-exclusion (Rezex ROA / Aminex HPX-87H, 5 mM H2SO4, 50 degC) or IC with suppressed conductivity
analytes: formic, acetic, lactic, citric, malic, quinic
decision_informed: Distinguishes true acid generation (formic/acetic rise = degradation) from perceived-sourness change driven only by CO2 loss.

method: Glass electrode, 3-point calibrated, at 20.0 +/- 0.5 degC, measured WITHOUT degassing and repeated after 10 min sparge with N2
decision_informed: Dissolved CO2 depresses pH, so as-is pH conflates carbonation with acid chemistry. Reporting both separates them. Also the safety-track input: pH >4.6 confirms TCS/ROP status.

method: Automatic titration with 0.1 M NaOH to pH 8.10 endpoint, on the degassed aliquot from N5
decision_informed: Perceived sourness driver; pairs with N4 to say whether acidity moved.

method: Digital refractometer (ATC), Brix reading x 0.85 espresso correction factor; sample cooled to 20 degC and filtered through 0.45 um to remove fines (fines bias the reading upward)
decision_informed: Go/no-go process control on extraction. Phase 0: frost dilution shifts TDS by -0.14% relative, >10x below the ~5% JND, so TDS is a BATCH control here, not a treatment endpoint.

method: EY% = TDS% x beverage mass (g) / dry dose (g)
decision_informed: Go/no-go: batch admitted only if EY 18-22% and within 1.0% absolute of the session median.

method: NON-INVASIVE optical/luminescent sensor spot (PSt3-class, 0-100% a.s.) bonded to the INNER wall before filling, interrogated through the glass by fibre-optic polymer probe. Two-point calibration (0% Na2SO3, 100% air-saturated), temperature-compensated from a co-located Pt100.
sample_prep: NONE - zero sample removed, zero air introduced, SAME vessel re-read at every timepoint
decision_informed: THE ASSAY THAT VALIDATES THE PACKAGING CLAIM. Clark electrodes and Winkler titration are EXCLUDED: both consume O2 and require decanting, which entrains the very analyte being measured. The non-invasive spot converts DO from a single destructive endpoint into a continuous ingress trajectory on every vessel in the trial.

method: Second optical O2 spot in the headspace of the same vessel, same read-out instrument
decision_informed: Verifies the <1% O2 flush AT SEAL (go/no-go) and detects septum/closure ingress over 48 h. Together with P1 it tells you whether a high DO came from a bad flush or a leaking seal.

method: Optical pCO2 spot in headspace + Henry's law at measured T; confirmatory by multiple-volume-expansion carbonation meter (CarboQC-class) on the destructive aliquot with piercing device
decision_informed: Quantifies the crema/effervescence loss Phase 0 predicts (~25% survival, undersaturated on collection). Sets the CO2 dose the service-point regeneration step has to add back.

method: Nephelometry (ISO 7027, 860 nm), on gently inverted then 60 s settled sample
sample_prep: 5 mL, or through-wall on the sealed vessel where geometry allows
decision_informed: Colloid stability. Pairs with P5 to date the onset of visible sediment.

method: Laser diffraction (Mie, RI 1.47/0.01, water dispersant), sample gently homogenised before aspiration
decision_informed: Phase 0: fines >20 um settle within ~1.2 h, i.e. visible sediment INSIDE the service hour. Loss of the >20 um mode over time is the quantitative sediment clock and drives whether the product needs re-agitation at service.

method: Spectrophotometer, transmission on 1:10 dilution in a 10 mm cuvette, D65/10 deg, CIELAB
analytes: L*, a*, b*, dE*ab vs t=0
decision_informed: Oxidative browning + sediment-driven lightening. Cheap orthogonal check on the oxidation index; a visible dE >2 is also a sensory confound the panel must be blinded against (opaque cups).

method: Hexanal and nonanal from the V1 SPME panel, ISTD-normalised
decision_informed: Lipid oxidation onset. This REPLACES PV/TBARS as the primary route: at 0.4-1.1 g/L lipid, a 90 mL vessel yields only 36-99 mg of lipid, so a peroxide value would consume the entire vessel for one number with poor precision.

method: Peroxide value, IDF/ferrous-oxidation spectrophotometric micro-method on lipid recovered by liquid-liquid extraction
sample_prep: Requires a DEDICATED extra vessel; ~50 mL to recover sufficient lipid
decision_informed: CONDITIONAL - run only at t=0 and t=48 h, and only if P7 shows a >2x between-arm hexanal difference. Otherwise dropped: it informs no decision that P7 does not inform more sensitively and more cheaply.

method: ISO 4833-1 pour plate, PCA, 30 degC / 72 h
decision_informed: Safety-track support and a spoilage veto on sensory tasting. A vessel exceeding 1e4 cfu/mL is withdrawn from the sensory panel.

method: Chilled-mirror dewpoint aw meter, 25 degC
sample_prep: 5 mL, ONCE PER BATCH not per timepoint
decision_informed: Documents the aw ~0.99 / pH ~5.15 combination that makes this a TCS food under reduced-oxygen packaging. Required evidence for the HACCP file; NOT a treatment endpoint.
